title: Request → Policy Check → Slack Approval → Execute

sections.label: 1 · REQUEST
sections.note: Requests arrive from a form or another system and are normalised into one shape, so the approval logic does not care where a request came from.

sections.label: 2 · POLICY
sections.note: Anything under the auto-approve threshold and inside policy clears without a human. The point of an approval workflow is to stop routing the routine 80% to a person.

sections.label: 3 · HUMAN GATE
sections.note: Everything else posts to Slack with Approve and Reject buttons and the full context attached. The workflow waits on the response rather than firing and hoping.

sections.label: 4 · EXECUTE
sections.note: Approved requests execute and the requester is told. Rejections are recorded with the reason, so the audit trail answers "who approved this and when" without anyone digging through Slack history.

input_sample.justification: Expedited shipping for the Ridgeline install — original carrier missed the window.

output_sample.note: Approved — confirmed the original carrier failure with ops before signing off.
